module_summary: vmc_groups.cpp is upstream Open PS2 Loader data: 97 shared memory-card groups (XEBP_100.xx, XEBP_000.xx) listing 1046 title IDs, with getGroupIdForTitleId doing a linear exact strcmp search; guigame.cpp uses it to name VMCs and for auto-VMC at launch. vmcsaves.cpp (first-party, ported from RIPPS2) treats a VMC image as a folder: it parses the superblock, indirect FAT and FAT, lists root saves with their icon.sys titles, copies a save between a card image, a save folder on the drive and a .psu file, and deletes a save, writing in a power-cut-safe order; it is driven synchronously by the VMC > Saves dialog (guigame.cpp) and the File Manager PSU paste (guifilemgr.cpp). xparam.cpp (upstream, krat0s) applies DECKARD (slim PS2) XPARAM emulation parameters by loading rom0:XPARAM or rom0:XPARAM2 with argument strings, once at boot (defaults) and once per game launch.

reusable_helpers.name: vsReadAll
reusable_helpers.what: reads exactly size bytes from an fd in 64 KB pieces, 0 on a short read

reusable_helpers.name: vsWriteAll
reusable_helpers.what: writes exactly size bytes to an fd in 64 KB pieces, 0 on a short write

reusable_helpers.name: vsStamp
reusable_helpers.what: time_t to an 8-byte memory-card date stamp (sceMcStDateTime, Japan time)

reusable_helpers.name: vmcSavesTitle
reusable_helpers.what: icon.sys header to its two-line title as plain ASCII (Shift-JIS full-width letters and punctuation mapped)

reusable_helpers.name: vsU32
reusable_helpers.what: little-endian u32 from a byte pointer

reusable_helpers.name: getGroupIdForTitleId
reusable_helpers.what: title ID to shared VMC group ID, or the input pointer when none

findings.title: vmcsaves: names read from a VMC image are not validated before vsWriteFolder joins them into a path, so an export can write outside SAVES/
findings.problem: vsLoadVmc copies the save name (453) and every file name (469) straight from the card's directory entries, and vsWriteFolder joins them into parent + save + '/' + file (727, 739) and opens that with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC (740). vsLoadPsu checks the same names with vsNameOk (796, 822) and vsWritePsu checks the save name (867), but the VMC-to-folder export (vmcSavesExport, guigame.cpp:442) checks nothing. A crafted VMC whose save holds a file named like '../../../X' makes the export create or truncate X outside the save folder on a device whose path layer resolves '..'.
findings.fix: Check the names where they enter, as vsLoadPsu does: in vsLoadVmc fail with VMCSAVES_ERR_NAME when vsNameOk(s->name) or vsNameOk(f->name) is false. The save-name check in vsWritePsu (867-868) then covers every source (folder and PSU sources are already checked) and can be deleted.
findings.justification: Adds two checks with an existing helper: they close a path traversal from untrusted VMC images (shared save cards) into the rest of the drive, and the now-redundant check in vsWritePsu goes, so the net change is about one line.
findings.benefit: Closes an overwrite-outside-the-folder path on VMC export (HDD/SMB/NFS); net about +1 line (INFERRED: +3 in vsLoadVmc, -2 in vsWritePsu).
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 440-491 (vsLoadVmc, no name check), 720-751 (vsWriteFolder joins s->name and f->name), 766-770 (vsNameOk), 780-843 (vsLoadPsu checks at 796 and 822), 860-868 (vsWritePsu: comment says a card name like ../x never leaves the folder). Caller guigame.cpp:442 vmcSavesExport(card, vmcSavesCard[pick].name, folder) with folder = <card dir>SAVES/ built at guigame.cpp:420. USB/MX4SIO go through FatFs with FF_FS_RPATH 0 (modules/bdm/bdmfs_fatfs/fatfs/include/ffconf.h:156), which rejects '..', so the exposed devices are pfs (HDD), SMB and NFS: INFERRED that those resolve '..' (pfs keeps '..' directory entries; its source is not in this repo).

findings.title: vmcSavesDelete frees at most 64 file chains, leaking card space for bigger saves; its files[] buffer is not needed
findings.problem: vmcSavesDelete collects file chains into u32_t files[SAVE_FILES] and stops at 64 (1181-1182, 1193); files past the 64th, and sub-folders inside the save (only MC_FILE is taken, 1194), are never freed, so once the root entry is hidden (1197-1198) their clusters stay marked used with nothing naming them. The buffer exists to free chains after the entry is hidden, but vsFreeChain and vsSetFat (300-304, 406-415) only change the in-memory FAT until vsFlushFat (1205), so freeing inside the scan keeps the same on-disk order.
findings.fix: Call vsFreeChain(&v, e.cluster) inside the scan loop for every existing file with length > 0 (keep the length test: an empty file's cluster field is 0, vsWriteVmc line 585), and delete files[], nfiles, the 64 cap and the second loop. Sub-folders inside a save stay unsupported, as they already are for export.
findings.benefit: Deleting a save with more than 64 files no longer loses VMC space until a reformat; ~5 lines and a 256 B stack array removed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 1176-1208, 275-304 and 406-415: vsFreeChain edits only v->fat and fatDirty; the only disk write before vsFlushFat is the hidden root entry at 1198, and an error return before the flush discards in-memory changes in vsClose. vsLoadVmc refuses saves over 64 files (464-467), so such saves can be deleted but not exported. Caller: guigame.cpp:467 after a confirm box. How often real saves exceed 64 files is not verified (INFERRED rare), hence Med confidence.

findings.title: vsIo seeks and transfers each 512-byte page separately even on images without ECC, doubling the I/O calls of every card-image access on the GUI thread
findings.problem: vsIo issues one lseek plus one read or write per page, ppc times per cluster. Without the ECC spare (raw == pageLen, the only kind that can be written, 238-241) a cluster's pages are contiguous, so one lseek and one transfer of csize bytes does the same. Every directory entry (vsEnt 316-329), FAT cluster (vsOpen 265, vsFlushFat 281) and data cluster (vsReadChain 366, vsWriteVmc 553 and 589) goes through it, synchronously from the VMC Saves dialog loop (guigame.cpp:435-474) on the GUI thread, which shows nothing while a copy runs.
findings.fix: In vsIo, when v->ecc is 0, do one lseek to abs * csize and one read or write of csize bytes; keep the per-page loop only for ECC images.
findings.justification: Adds one branch: it halves the lseek/read/write calls (each a fileXio RPC on the PS2, INFERRED) for standard 2-page clusters, which is the main cost of copying a large save while the UI is frozen; it adds no state.
findings.benefit: Calls per 1 KB cluster 4 -> 2: an 8 MB save export drops from ~32 K to ~16 K calls (INFERRED: 8192 clusters x 2 pages x 2 calls); listing and FAT loads halve too.
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 173-184, 198-273, 316-329, 358-374, 494-629: page p of cluster abs is at offset (abs*ppc+p)*raw, contiguous when raw == pageLen; ECC images are refused for writing at 238-241. Callers: guigame.cpp:377, 422, 439-467 call vmcSaves* inside the diaExecuteDialog loop at 435 (GUI thread). That each newlib call is one fileXio RPC, and its cost, is INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: vmcsaves holds 4.9 KB of .bss for the whole run: vsCopy's static vs_save_t and vsWritePsu's static pad
findings.problem: vsCopy's static vs_save_t s (1123; 3896 B, not the ~2.5 KB its comment says) and vsWritePsu's static pad[1024] (862) are used only during one copy but stay in .bss for the whole run; vmcsaves.o has 4924 B of .bss. Both run on GUI code paths whose thread stack is 128 KB.
findings.fix: Drop the two static keywords so both live on the stack during the copy (the memsets at 1127 and 881 already initialise them) and correct the size in the comment.
findings.benefit: 4920 B of RAM freed (MEASURED: riptopl-per-object.tsv vmcsaves.o bss 4924; nm sizes vsCopy::s 0xf38, vsWritePsu::pad 0x400); peak stack grows by 4.9 KB of 128 KB.
findings.evidence: evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt: _ZZL6vsCopyiPKcS0_iS0_E1s size 0xf38 and _ZZL10vsWritePsuPK9vs_save_tPKcE3pad size 0x400; riptopl-per-object.tsv: vmcsaves.o bss 4924; riptopl-stack-heap.txt: main ELF _stack_size 0x20000. Callers: VMC Saves dialog (guigame.cpp:439-467) and File Manager paste (guifilemgr.cpp:448, 452, 559), INFERRED main thread. Deepest path: vsCopy (s) -> vsWriteVmc (about 2 KB of entries and first[]) or vsWritePsu (pad, two path buffers).

findings.title: vsLoadFolder stats every file twice and keeps a separate malloc'd name list
findings.problem: The readdir pass stats each entry (660) and copies its name into a malloc'd list (645-647, 667); the second pass rebuilds the same path and stats it again only for st_mtime (702-705). On a real memory card (File Manager Paste as PSU, guifilemgr.cpp:448) each stat is a card directory lookup. The list also costs a malloc and eight free(list) calls on the error paths.
findings.fix: In the first pass write the name, and the stamp from the stat already made, straight into s->files[names] (count still advances only once data is allocated, so vsSaveFree is unaffected; set s->created before the loop for the fallback), then delete list, its malloc, its frees and the second stat.
findings.benefit: One stat per file saved (up to 64 per save); ~13 lines removed (INFERRED from lines 636, 645-647, eight free(list) lines and 702-705, minus 2 added).
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 633-716 and 136-143 (vsSaveFree frees files[0..count-1] only). free(list) at 651, 664, 672, 683, 689, 697, 709, 714. Callers: vmcSavesImport (guigame.cpp:457) and vmcSavesFolderToPsu (guifilemgr.cpp:448).

findings.title: vmc_groups: eight malformed title IDs never match, and groups XEBP_100.72 and XEBP_000.12 are unreachable duplicates
findings.problem: getGroupIdForTitleId compares exact strings (1465) with IDs like SLUS_207.54 passed by guigame.cpp:493, 529 and 702, but lines 443-444, 464-465, 472-473, 498 and 614 hold SLUS_20754, SLUS_20824, SCES_50422, SLES_50422, SCES_51154, SLES_51154, SLES-5350 and SSCES_540.95, so those games get their own VMC name instead of their series card. Group 100.72 (1149-1152) repeats 100.71 (1143-1146), and all four titles of 000.12 (1272-1275) are also in 100.53 (936-939); the first match wins, so 100.72 and 000.12 are never returned.
findings.fix: Correct the eight strings to the 11-character form (SLUS_207.54, SLUS_208.24, SCES_504.22, SLES_504.22, SCES_511.54, SLES_511.54, most likely SLES_535.06, SCES_540.95). Delete group 100.72 (1149-1153 and its row at 1424), and either delete 000.12 (1271-1276 and row 1439) or move its four titles out of 100.53, whichever upstream intended. The table is upstream Open PS2 Loader data, so the fix belongs upstream too.
findings.benefit: Eight title IDs regain their series VMC name in the VMC dialog and auto-VMC; 13 lines removed with the two unreachable groups (no behaviour change for those).
findings.evidence: awk over vmc_groups.cpp for title strings not shaped XXXX_NNN.NN: only the eight lines cited. Duplicate scan: 1150-1152 equal 1144-1146, 1272-1275 equal 936-939, plus five harmless repeats inside one group (665/668, 675/676, 1028/1029, 1053/1057, 1222/1226). tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:15-17 calls these a known data issue and does not assert them. git log --follow: from upstream 48da113d (VMC Group Support, #1547) and e53edb28 (#1594). Callers pass the startup ID copied from config or the game list (guigame.cpp:521-529, 696-702).

findings.title: vmc_groups: 1046 per-title pointers cost 4184 B of .data; fixed-width char arrays make them unnecessary
findings.problem: Each of the 97 groups is a static const char *titles_*[] array (first at line 14, last at 1346), so every title costs a 4-byte pointer in .data on top of its 12-byte string: vmc_groups.o has 4184 B of .data = 1046 x 4. Every ID is 11 characters (once SSCES_540.95 at 614 is fixed, finding 6), so the pointers carry no information.
findings.fix: Declare each group as static const char titles_*[][12] with the same initialiser lists and make MemoryCardGroup.titleIds a const char (*)[12]; the count expressions, the strcmp lookup and the host test keep working. A mechanical edit of 97 declarations and one struct field.
findings.benefit: ~4 KB of ELF and RAM (MEASURED 4184 B .data in riptopl-per-object.tsv; strings move from .rodata.str into the arrays at the same 12 B, minus ~144 B of string merging lost for 12 repeated IDs, INFERRED).
findings.evidence: evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-per-object.tsv: vmc_groups.o text 224, rodata 1164 (allMemoryCardGroups, nm size 0x48c = 97 x 12), data 4184. grep -cE over indented string lines of vmc_groups.cpp: 1046 titles. tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:22-28 reads g.titleIds[j] into a const char *, which an array row decays to. The 12-character SSCES_540.95 would not fit a [12] row, so finding 6 comes first.
